title: Rental Operations
business_context: A fictional equipment-rental provider wants to understand inspection workload and turnaround after returns. Identify useful patterns, check whether averages alone are informative, and recommend where operations managers should investigate.
learner_profile: Business-school introductory analytics students with limited programming experience.
ai_policy: AI tools are allowed throughout. You remain responsible for your data handling, evidence, and conclusions.

learning_objectives.description: Frame useful business questions and explain the comparisons selected.
Guide AI exploration and verify the calculations supporting a finding.
Communicate evidence-based recommendations and distinguish observations from causal hypotheses.

columns.name: TurnaroundHours
columns.description: Hours from return to availability for the next rental

columns.name: RepairNeeded
columns.description: Whether return inspection identified a repair need

patterns.title: Duration and turnaround
patterns.business_question: Do long rentals require longer turnaround after return?
patterns.generation_rule: Turnaround includes a quadratic duration component and service-level adjustment.
patterns.interaction_policy: Service tier adds variation; compare the duration groups and inspect possible tier differences.
patterns.interpretation_limits: A median gap does not alone establish a quadratic shape or the causal effect of extending one rental. Inspect a duration plot before making a shape claim.

patterns.title: Equipment-specific repair rates
patterns.business_question: Which equipment groups need more inspection attention?
patterns.generation_rule: Use a higher repair probability for PowerTool rentals.
patterns.interaction_policy: Repair assignment is separate from duration and turnaround in this teaching scenario.
patterns.interpretation_limits: No repair cost, staffing cost, or safety incident outcome is measured.

checks.description: Median turnaround-hour difference: rentals at least 20 days minus rentals at most 5 days
Repair-share difference: PowerTool minus other equipment

requirements: Support at least two operational findings with appropriate visualizations.
For one finding, explain a robust summary such as a median and compare it with a mean.
Write a recommendation that acknowledges what the synthetic records do not measure.

criteria.name: Analytical evidence
criteria.description: Full credit requires the case's major relationships, correct comparisons and denominators, and reproducible evidence. Award proportional credit for independently supported partial findings; unsupported claims earn no discovery credit.

criteria.name: Business interpretation
criteria.description: Recommendations follow the evidence, acknowledge unmeasured explanations, and explain business relevance. Reduce credit for unsupported mechanisms or irrelevant recommendations.

criteria.name: Communication
criteria.description: Charts are appropriate, clearly labeled, and accompanied by concise interpretations that meet the assignment requirements. Award partial credit according to clarity and completeness.

notes: Count duplicate conclusions once, even when visualized differently.
Review valid unlisted findings on their evidence and relevance; they are not automatically false positives.
The key is not exhaustive. These proposed descriptors require instructor review before actual grading.
